prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the large concrete/plastered surface very close in front of and above the camera wearer, roughly 0.3–1 m away, while the scaffolding, floor, and scattered construction objects lie farther ahead and below, mostly about 1.5–5 m away. It makes the surface’s strong foreground occlusion and the gaps opening beneath it clearer than RGB alone; across the five frames, its nearest region shifts from upper left/centre toward the right as the wearer turns or moves around it. Poles and rails cross one another at several depths, but their thin geometry is inconsistently estimated, and the people visible near the far left in frame 1 and upper middle-left in frame 5 are not cleanly separated from their surroundings. Absolute metre values are uncertain because this is monocular relative depth, and several bright bands and dark regions appear smoothed or discontinuous at object edges.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies only two person instances: one partly cut off at the far left edge of frame 1 and one near the upper-left/centre of frame 5, both several metres from the camera wearer, with no person masks in frames 2–4. In RGB context, each person stands beyond the close wall and among the scaffolding, so neither is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach; they are never visible together in one frame, so their separation cannot be measured reliably. The first person is mostly side-on or oblique and heavily cropped, while the fifth-frame person is small and distant; the masks do not provide enough detail to establish gaze direction confidently. This map makes the people easier to localize against the clutter, but it misses the concrete surface, rails, tools, bags, bucket-like objects, and other scene structure, and both person masks are incomplete because of cropping, distance, or occlusion.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains no detected body or hand skeletons in any of the five frames, so it supplies no reliable evidence about limb positions, facing direction, gaze, interpersonal orientation, or arm’s-reach relationships. In RGB, distant people are visible in frames 1 and 5, but they are small, partly cropped or obstructed by scaffolding and the close concrete surface, which likely prevents pose recovery. The empty map therefore cannot track approach, retreat, or turning across time, nor can it distinguish whether either person faces toward or away from the camera wearer. Its main spatial indication is negative and unreliable: no usable body or hand keypoints were recovered, not that people or hands are absent from the scene.
